title: Cisco CCST Cybersecurity (100-160) Study Guide
description: The Cisco Certified Support Technician (CCST) Cybersecurity is Cisco's $125 entry security cert — 50 minutes, no prerequisites, and backed by the most substantial free entry-level cyber curriculum from any vendor (NetAcad's 120-hour Junior Cybersecurity Analyst path). Honest framing: it's a learning checkpoint, not a job ticket.
audience: Students and absolute beginners pivoting toward security with zero background. If you're mid-career and need a security job soon, this isn't your cert — Security+ is. This is the ground-floor option for people building from nothing on a budget.
why_get_it: The strongest reason isn't the cert — it's the curriculum behind it. NetAcad's Junior Cybersecurity Analyst path is 120 free hours of genuinely solid security fundamentals: security principles, network security, endpoint concepts, vulnerability assessment, incident handling. The $125 exam is a confidence checkpoint that proves the material stuck. What it is not: a SOC-job credential. 'Entry-level cybersecurity job' barely exists, and the postings that do exist screen for Security+ (DoD 8140-approved — CCST is not), a degree, or experience. Take this cert with clear eyes: it's the cheapest structured start in security, and the road continues through networking fundamentals and Security+ before a SOC seat is realistic.
when_to_get_it: When you're a student, when your school pays for it, or when you're at the very start of a self-funded pivot and want a milestone partway through the free NetAcad path. Skip it if you need a security job within a year — put the money toward Security+ instead (roughly 3× the cost, but it's the credential HR filters and government contracts actually require). And if you're drawn to security through networking, consider CCST Networking → CCNA → security instead; defenders who understand networks outperform defenders who memorized threat lists.
salary_note: The honest version: CCST Cybersecurity alone does not get you a SOC analyst job. It feeds cyber-adjacent support roles — help desk with security duties, junior technician — around $40–58K U.S. Real entry SOC roles ($45–70K) typically want Security+, CCNA Cybersecurity, a degree, or internship experience on top. This cert is mile one of that road, priced accordingly.
exam_format: 40–50 questions (multiple choice plus performance-based items), via Certiport testing centers or Pearson VUE (test center or OnVUE online). Unlimited retakes, instant results. Passing score not published.
recertification_note: Same 2025 policy change as all CCSTs: earned on/after July 15, 2025 = 5-year validity; before = lifetime. Renew only by passing any current CCST or higher Cisco exam — CE credits don't apply at this tier.

items: The CIA triad and core security vocabulary
Common threats: malware, phishing, social engineering
Network security basics: firewalls, VPNs, secure protocols
Host-based protections: antimalware, host firewalls, hardening
Operating system security basics across Windows and Linux
Patch management and why unpatched systems get owned
Detecting suspicious behavior on an endpoint
The endpoint's place in the bigger defensive picture
Vulnerability management concepts and risk basics
The incident response lifecycle at ground level
Escalation, documentation, and evidence handling basics
Writing up what happened so the next tier can act

study_steps.title: Start the free Junior Cybersecurity Analyst path
study_steps.description: NetAcad's 120-hour path is the official prep and the most substantial free entry cyber curriculum anywhere. It IS the product — the exam just certifies you finished it with understanding. Budget 2–4 months at a steady pace.

study_steps.title: Pull the official blueprint
study_steps.description: Download the 100-160 exam topics from the Cisco Learning Network. Five domains, no published weights (Cisco doesn't publish them for CCST — ignore invented percentages). Use it to track coverage as you work through the path.

study_steps.title: Add the Endpoint Security mini-course
study_steps.description: NetAcad's free 27-hour Endpoint Security course maps directly onto domain 3 and adds hands-on depth the main path treats more lightly. Free reinforcement — take it.

study_steps.title: Get free hands-on reps outside the courseware
study_steps.description: TryHackMe's free intro rooms turn the concepts into practice — and give you something concrete to mention when the cert alone doesn't impress. A beginner who can say 'here's my TryHackMe profile' beats one with only a badge.

study_steps.title: Demo the exam interface, then book
study_steps.description: Certiport's free Test Drive shows the real interface. Then book via Certiport (through schools) or Pearson VUE (test center or online). 50 minutes, instant result, unlimited retakes — deliberately low stakes.

study_steps.title: Plan the road past this cert honestly
study_steps.description: CCST Cybersecurity is mile one. The realistic sequence to a SOC seat runs through networking fundamentals (CCST Networking or Network+), then Security+ — the DoD-approved HR-filter cert — then hands-on labs and often an IT support rung. Our SOC Analyst path lays out the whole road.

faq.question: Will CCST Cybersecurity get me a SOC job?
faq.answer: No — and any site implying otherwise is selling you something. Entry SOC postings screen for Security+, CCNA Cybersecurity, degrees, or experience. CCST Cybersecurity is mile one: the cheapest structured start, backed by excellent free training, on a road that realistically runs through Security+ and often an IT support rung first. Our SOC Analyst career path maps the honest route.

faq.question: CCST Cybersecurity or Security+ — which should I take?
faq.answer: If you need a security-relevant credential for job applications: Security+, no contest — it's DoD 8140-approved and the keyword filters search for it, at roughly 3× the price. CCST is for an earlier moment: students, tight budgets, or testing whether security genuinely pulls you before committing real money. Many people do CCST's free path first, then spend on Security+ with confidence.

faq.question: Is this the same as CCNA Cybersecurity?
faq.answer: No — different tiers. CCST Cybersecurity ($125, entry) is the beginner checkpoint. CCNA Cybersecurity ($300, associate — formerly CyberOps Associate, renamed February 2026) is the SOC-focused associate cert that actually appears in some analyst postings. Cisco positions CCST as the stepping stone toward it, but no exam credit transfers.

faq.question: Does it expire?
faq.answer: Earned before July 15, 2025: lifetime. On or after: 5 years, renewable only by passing any current CCST or higher Cisco exam. CE credits don't apply at this tier.

faq.question: What's actually on the exam?
faq.answer: Five domains: security principles, network security concepts, endpoint security, vulnerability assessment and risk, and incident handling. 40–50 questions in 50 minutes, including performance-based items. It tests the fundamentals the 120-hour path teaches — no exotic content, no trick depth.
